title: Forsythia suspensa accelerates wound healing by inhibiting neutrophil extracellular traps and activating Wnt/beta-catenin via forsythoside A.
authors: Zhi, Guoguo; Shen, Haiyu; Li, Zihao; Che, Manju; Cheng, Lin; Du, Zhirui; Yan, Xueqiao; Zhang, Shaoyang; Yang, Ruichen; Ma, Xiuying; Liu, Huijuan; Geng, Funeng; Li, Baojie
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究连翘促进皮肤伤口愈合的分子机制，涉及NETs和Wnt信号通路，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cutaneous wound repair is a complex biological process that restores the integrity of the skin. Forsythia suspensa (LQ) is a traditional Chinese medicinal herb known for its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties; however, its role and molecular mechanisms in promoting cutaneous tissue regeneration remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the pharmacological efficacy of LQ and its bioactive compounds in treating acute skin injuries and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. METHOD: Two distinct animal models, a full-thickness thermal injury wound (complex inflammatory damage) and a full-thickness excisional wound (mechanical trauma), were established to evaluate the therapeutic potential of LQ. Therapeutic effects were assessed by histopathological examination and immunofluorescence analysis of skin lesions. RNA sequencing and pathway-specific inhibitors were used to investigate and validate the molecular mechanisms involved. Active compounds were identified by UPLC-MS/MS, and their mechanisms of action were explored using molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and experimental validation. RESULTS: LQ significantly accelerates cutaneous wound healing in both models. Mechanistically, LQ promotes tissue regeneration by suppressing neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation and activating Wnt/beta-catenin signaling to drive epidermal cell proliferation, and these effects are reversed by the NET inhibitor GSK484 and the Wnt pathway inhibitor IWP2. Forsythoside A, an active component of LQ, similarly enhances wound closure, re-epithelialization, and cell proliferation, indicating that it is likely the key mediator. We further show that inhibition of NETs increases Wnt ligand production and beta-catenin signaling, linking inflammatory responses to regenerative signaling. CONCLUSION: LQ and forsythoside A promote skin wound healing by coordinately regulating NET-mediated inflammation and Wnt/beta-catenin signaling-mediated cell proliferation, thereby highlighting their potential as therapeutic agents in regenerative medicine.
abstract_zh: 背景：皮肤创面修复是一个复杂的生物学过程，旨在恢复皮肤的完整性。连翘（LQ）是一种传统中草药，以其抗炎和抗菌特性而闻名；然而，其在促进皮肤组织再生中的作用及分子机制尚不清楚。目的：本研究旨在评估LQ及其生物活性化合物在治疗急性皮肤损伤中的药理学功效，并阐明其潜在分子机制。方法：建立两种不同的动物模型，即全层热损伤创面（复杂炎症损伤）和全层切除创面（机械创伤），以评估LQ的治疗潜力。通过皮肤病变的组织病理学检查和免疫荧光分析评估治疗效果。使用RNA测序和通路特异性抑制剂来研究和验证所涉及的分子机制。通过UPLC-MS/MS鉴定活性化合物，并利用分子对接、分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟和实验验证探索其作用机制。结果：LQ在两种模型中均显著加速皮肤创面愈合。机制上，LQ通过抑制中性粒细胞胞外陷阱 (neutrophil extracellular trap, NET) 形成并激活Wnt/β-catenin信号通路以驱动表皮细胞增殖，从而促进组织再生，而这些效应可被NET抑制剂GSK484和Wnt通路抑制剂IWP2逆转。连翘酯苷A（Forsythoside A）作为LQ的活性成分，同样增强创面闭合、再上皮化和细胞增殖，表明其可能是关键介导因子。我们进一步证明，抑制NETs会增加Wnt配体产生和β-catenin信号传导，将炎症反应与再生信号联系起来。结论：LQ和连翘酯苷A通过协调调节NET介导的炎症和Wnt/β-catenin信号介导的细胞增殖来促进皮肤创面愈合，从而凸显其在再生医学中作为治疗剂的潜力。
